defs: very bad or awful
not good at all
really bad and unpleasant
exs: The weather was terrible, so we stayed home.
I had a terrible dream last night.
This soup tastes terrible. I can't eat it.

defs: cloth that opens and closes on a stage
a big cloth that hides the stage
cloth that hangs to cover a window
exs: The curtain opened and the play began.
Mom closed the curtain to keep the sun out.
Behind the curtain, the actors waited quietly.

defs: was right to get something because of what one did
earned something because of what you did
was right to get something, whether good or bad
exs: Tom worked hard, so he deserved the prize.
The boy broke the toy, so he deserved the blame.
Our team played well and deserved to win.

defs: in a big, showy way like an actor
with big, exciting actions or words
in a way that is too big and loud
exs: The girl dramatically fell to the floor in the play.
He dramatically opened the door and shouted, "Surprise!"
She dramatically cried when she lost her pen.

defs: a feeling of being ill
when your body does not feel well
a problem that makes you feel bad
exs: I missed school because of sickness.
The car ride gave me a little sickness.
Her sickness went away after she slept.

defs: a vehicle that flies to other planets
a machine that travels in space
a vehicle that travels through space
exs: The spaceship flew past the moon.
He drew a red spaceship on his paper.
In the movie, a spaceship landed in the park.

defs: to make something bad or not fun
to ruin a good thing
to make a plan go wrong
exs: Rain can spoil our picnic.
Please don't spoil the movie by telling the end.
Loud noise will spoil my nap.

defs: making people come close to look
pulling people toward something
getting people to come and watch
exs: The big sale is attracting many shoppers.
Bright lights are attracting bugs to the lamp.
The singer is attracting a lot of fans.

defs: a shop that sells things to make money
work of buying and selling
a place that sells things to people
exs: My uncle has a small bakery business.
Business is good when many people come to the shop.
She wants to start her own business someday.

defs: thin, dry snacks that go well with cheese
small, crisp snacks
flat, crunchy food made from flour
exs: I ate cheese and crackers after school.
Mom put crackers in my lunch box.
The soup came with a bag of crackers.

defs: a large group of people in one place
many people together
a lot of people standing close
exs: A big crowd watched the school play.
There was a crowd at the zoo on Sunday.
The crowd clapped when the team won.

defs: to get money for doing work
to get pay for a job
to get money by working
exs: Dad works hard to earn money for our family.
I want to earn some money by washing cars.
Kids can earn a star by cleaning the room.

defs: more than the usual amount
added to what you already have
more than needed
exs: I need an extra pencil for the test.
Grandma gave me extra candy on my birthday.
We have an extra seat at our table.

defs: a store that sells food and home things
a shop for milk, fruit and bread
a place to buy food
exs: Mom went to the grocery store to buy milk.
The grocery near my house sells fresh fruit.
We bought eggs and bread at the grocery.

defs: the body parts at the sides below your waist
the parts you move when you dance
the body parts between your waist and legs
exs: She put her hands on her hips and smiled.
The dancer moved her hips to the music.
My belt sits on my hips.

defs: in a way that wishes for a good result
with a wish that something good will happen
wishing for a good answer
exs: The puppy looked at me hopefully for a snack.
"Can I go play?" she asked hopefully.
He waited hopefully for his test score.

defs: to speak in a low voice that is hard to hear
to talk softly and not clearly
to say words in a quiet, unclear way
exs: Please don't mumble. I can't hear you.
He began to mumble when he felt shy.
Grandpa likes to mumble while he reads.

defs: small amounts of food to try for free
small parts that show what something is like
little pieces given so you can try them
exs: The shop gave out free samples of cake.
We tried samples of juice at the store.
Mom looked at paint samples for my room.

defs: a machine that makes sound louder
a loud box that sends out voices or music
a thing that plays sound for many people
exs: A voice came from the speaker in the store.
The speaker on my phone is very loud.
The teacher spoke through a speaker in the hall.
